title: EEG During Mental Arithmetic Tasks
description: This dataset comprises scalp EEG recordings from 36 healthy university students during resting-state and mental arithmetic task conditions. Participants performed serial subtraction tasks while 23-channel EEG was recorded at 500 Hz using the International 10/20 electrode placement system. The dataset is designed to investigate neural correlates of cognitive workload and mathematical cognition, with applications in cognitive neuroscience, mental workload assessment, and brain-computer interface research.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a Neurocom 23-channel monopolar system sampled at 500 Hz with electrodes placed according to the International 10/20 system and referenced to interconnected ear electrodes. Filters included a high-pass filter (0.5 Hz cut-off), low-pass filter (45 Hz cut-off), and power line notch filter (50 Hz). The protocol consisted of a 3-minute resting-state recording with eyes closed and a 4-minute mental arithmetic task involving serial subtraction. The dataset stores the last 3 minutes of the rest period and the first minute of mental arithmetic performance for each participant.
